Besieges; and thrice in the lowest whirlpool of her abyss the vast
She sucks the waves down into the sheer depth, and again into the air
She hurls them up in turn, and lashes the stars with the wave.
It is better to round the turning-posts of Trinacrian Pachynus
Delaying, and to bend your long courses around,
Than once to have seen, beneath her vast cave, misshapen
Scylla, and the rocks resounding with her sea-blue hounds.
Let not any of these losses of delay be of such great cost to you,
And in what way you may both shun and bear each labour;
I shall unfold, and, duly honoured, grant favourable courses.
These are the things of which you may be warned by my voice:
Only proceed, and where the way leads you, direct your step;
For by this way both your ships and the youth of your people,
Either hold the harbour, or enter the mouth under full sail.
MUSE.
It stands fixed to obey your warnings, my will is certain,
Great Mother of God, for me it is right to carry out your commands,
So that at last it may be granted to join right hand with right hand,
And to hear and return the auspicious voices of those above.
O fortunate ones, whose walls rise there:
But better is the lot of those whose fortune is accomplished
Already as their own. We are called from one fate to another:
For them rest is won, no expanse of sea to be ploughed;
Nor fields of Elysium, ever receding backward,
To be sought. Meanwhile happy, twice and thrice blessed,
Is he who, as soon as he looks up at the heights of that city,
Both hastens his way, and directs his step toward the walls;
Whom, as he walks, God has fenced about with a dark covering,
And, surrounding him, has poured a thick mantle of cloud over him,
So that no one may be able to see him, nor anyone to touch him,

div.note: * By the land on the right, understand the way of God's commandments, which leads to eternal life.
By the left side is signified the way of perdition, which consists in the transgression of the divine law.

lg.l: Or to contrive a delay, or to ask the reasons for coming.
Bring me in, I pray, O God most good, enclosed in this cloud,
So that nothing but the divine may remain stored up in my mind;
For my mind shudders to remember every profane kind:
Let the one image of God the dear Father come to mind,
And may I ponder the cruel fates of Christ alone;
May the great virtue of the man recur to my mind, and the great
Honor of his praise; may his features remain fixed in my breast,
He to me life, salvation, guide of life, the true of salvation
Path let him be; hereafter let mortal things touch me not at all,
and let death be gain to one who gazes on the heavenly kingdoms.
Long since worn out for the world, why do I, useless, the years
Delay? Ah, if only I might stand safe on my Father's threshold.
Let this be the final labor, this the goal of long journeys.
Behold, we have completed a plain immense in its distances,
And now it is time to unyoke the smoking necks of the horses;
* May God bring us, who departed from here, to auspicious shores.

div.note: * Through the fall of the first parents.

lg.l: PRAYER:
SOUL OF CHRIST, SANCTIFY ME.
Mind of Christ, restoring souls and fallen hearts,
make haste to repair the ruins of my fallen breast,
filling me with your divine presence as I wander through the empty void,
may I be adorned with Astraea and the rest of virtue's garment,
since the lofty glories of the supreme Father gather themselves together.
BODY OF CHRIST, SAVE ME.
The foul fluid of the heart has overflowed, and all
the bones, shaken by disease, are little by little drawn in upon themselves;
Nay, a parching fever rages and feeds within upon
the entrails scorched with thirst: manifold pain seizes the limbs.
What is left? Shall I pursue the healing arts of Apollo?
Should he bring the help of his art? It will avail nothing to have tried him.
Let your healing flesh, O Christ, be the cause of my salvation.
BLOOD OF CHRIST, INEBRIATE ME.
I seek your gatherings, O Christ, and the pleasant places of your people,
Assemblies, and the Elysian fields: hither chaste from bleeding
wines lead from your veins, with blood drawn forth.
Sweeter than unmixed wine itself to me is the wave of the rosy stream
of yours, O Christ: whom have these chalices not made eloquent?
Go far away, you cups of Bacchus that defile minds,
provided that these wines of honey-flowing blood gladden me.
WATER FROM THE SIDE OF CHRIST, WASH ME.
O pure liquid flowing from the wound of Christ's side,
wash away the dregs of deadly stain from our hearts,
for the door of the high King is open to no blemish.

div.note: Here the linking of virtues to one another is implied.

lg.l: PASSION OF CHRIST, STRENGTHEN ME.
The cruel scourges, the fierce blows of the spear-point driven in,
O Christ, to your flesh, on whose whole body no
lash is dealt in vain, may they strengthen me with mighty strength.
DEATH OF CHRIST, GIVE ME LIFE.
Your death is life to me, that my courage may be lively in war,
while we are surrounded on all sides by the arms of Cocytus;
Father, hurl your flames into our breasts,
us with the torch, us with the sword, us with the same wound, O victor,
consume; grant that the offspring may go as a companion to the dear parent.
We shall go to the desired death, with you as leader, a victim offered;
provided that your death brings forth life-giving beginnings for me.
O GOOD JESUS, HEAR ME.
O kindly guardian of your flock, most gentle Jesus,
Supreme Shepherd of the sheep, to whom so many sheepfolds are a care,
which your loving-kindness never passes by with a deaf ear,
do not, gentle one, refuse to heed the voices of those praying.
HIDE ME WITHIN YOUR WOUNDS.
Let the power be granted to have lain hidden in your wounds,
especially at the rosy threshold of the pierced heart,
for in these shores I shall always dwell safe,
until the grievous wickedness is washed away and expiated by a fountain of tears.
AND DO NOT SEPARATE ME FROM YOU, BUT PLACE ME BESIDE YOU.
May I be bound to you with so great a bond of love,
that I can never be torn away from your fatherly embraces,
either by any chance, or by any crisis of affairs,
while life is my companion, while breath shall rule these limbs,
and your loving-kindness claims me, ripe for Olympus.

div.n: VT CVM ANGELIS, ET SANCTIS TVIS, &c.

lg.l: THAT WITH THE ANGELS, AND THY SAINTS, etc.
Where it may at last be lawful for me to resume the sceptre of the kingdom.
And in return for His gifts, to render His dues to the Thunderer,
In the manner of the winged ones, with lyres and sounding strings,
And with the countless harmonies of voices, the halls of heaven
To fill, and joyful to say thrice 'Io', thrice 'Paean',
And, joined to the choirs of the Ones Above, the three faces of the Godhead
To behold, faces illuminated by the light of the Divine.
But indeed he is deemed to lead a happy life,
Who cannot satisfy his mind, and burns by gazing upon
A sight of that kind; standing fixed upon this one thing,
whereby it is granted to possess the heavenly lot forever.

div.n: MAGNIFICAT ANIMA MEA DOMINVM, ET EXVLTAVIT SPIRITVS MEVS, &c.

lg.l: MY SOUL MAGNIFIES THE LORD, AND MY SPIRIT HAS REJOICED, etc.
It is right to pay worthy thanks to the King of Heaven,
and to exult in our souls in God, for so great a gift,
with which His goodness deems us worthy, the pleasing of salvation
bringing gifts, when He destines His own offspring for the altar.
BECAUSE HE HAS REGARDED THE HUMILITY OF HIS HANDMAID.
He who looks down from on high upon the lowly lot of His handmaid,
and to dwell in humble cottages, and the hiding places of the womb
He does not shrink back at all, but becomes a new guest in these dwellings
by a virgin birth, with the undefiled flower of modesty,
resolving to make me a parent by a divine offspring,
hence I discharge no empty office of a Mother.
FOR BEHOLD, FROM HENCEFORTH ALL GENERATIONS SHALL CALL ME BLESSED.
Thenceforth every race of men me three and four times blessed
shall declare to be, giving me an eternal name for all ages:
As long as rivers shall run into the seas, as long as shadows on the mountains
shall traverse the slopes, while the sky feeds the stars,
forever shall my honor, and my name, and my praises remain.
HE WHO IS MIGHTY HAS DONE GREAT THINGS FOR ME.
You grant, O nurturing Father (who holds supreme power over the world),
that I may be not the lowest of the great Isaacid lineage of heroes,
glory, so that a single page may not confine my virtue.
Surely too great is the grace of my changed lot,
while it is enough for your handmaid, if you adorn her with the honors of praise.

div.n: ET SANCTVM NOMEN EIVS, ET MISERICORDIA EIVS A PROGENIE, &c.

lg.l: AND HOLY IS HIS NAME, AND HIS MERCY FROM GENERATION, etc.
Rightly is a holy name owed to you by your divine power,
Since your mercy, O King, pours itself out upon all
men distinguished by piety, upon whatever there is everywhere
of the race of saints, which is scattered through the great world,
and those whom time shall bring, and has brought, in whose heart manly
virtue has settled, to whom the fear of the Lord has added wings,
fear itself, the flanks of the foaming horse with spurs
while it digs, and forces it to run down rough paths.
HE HATH SHOWED MIGHT IN HIS ARM, HE HATH SCATTERED THE PROUD, etc.
The mighty right hand of the Lord, itself like a great army,
scatters breasts swelling with turgid pride.
As many as the waves that roll on the Libyan sea,
where fierce Orion is hidden in the wintry waves;
or as many as the thick ears of grain that are scorched by the early sun,
either on the plain of Hermus, or in the yellowing fields of Lycia:
so many necks of the proud does it lay low on the tawny sand,
the wrath of the supreme Godhead, truly mighty in war.
Let shields resound, and let the roused earth tremble with the beat of feet,
and let bronze shields flash, let the brazen sword flash;
in vain will the arms of the swelling ones rise up against the Powers above.
HE HATH PUT DOWN THE MIGHTY FROM THEIR SEAT, AND HATH EXALTED THE HUMBLE.
He who makes the lofty ash trees come down from the mountains,
will he not be able to thrust those holding the sublime scepters of the kingdom,
the proud in heart, down from their illustrious throne?
and on the other hand, to bear those lowly in spirit above the heavens?

div.n: ESVRIENTES IMPLEVIT BONIS, ET DIVITES DIMISIT INANES.

lg.l: HE HATH FILLED THE HUNGRY WITH GOOD THINGS, AND THE RICH HE HATH SENT EMPTY AWAY.
Is he not able to curb the hunger of the empty mind,
so that hunger is taken away, and the love of possessing held in check?
Nor by his power relieve the thirst of the thirsting miser?
And will he not be able to send away the rich in want of all things,
who once had been mighty with wide dominion?
A thousand ewe-lambs of yours now roam the Sicilian mountains,
fresh milk fails you neither in summer nor in the cold,
and perhaps tomorrow's light will see you stripped of your goods.
HE HATH RECEIVED ISRAEL HIS SERVANT, BEING MINDFUL OF HIS MERCY.
After so many thousand circuits, as the months rolled round,
mindful himself of his promise and of his ancestral mercy,
by which he willed to undo the common guilt of the world,
by a happy birth he is brought forth into the air of light,
in the manner of an infant, sprung from the blood of the sons of Isaac.
Come hither, O beautiful boy; for you lilies in full
baskets, behold, the Nymphs bring; for you the fair Naiad,
plucking pale violets and the tops of poppies,
joins the narcissus and the flower of sweet-smelling dill,
then, weaving them together with cassia and other sweet herbs,
she sets off the soft hyacinths with yellow marigold:
I myself will gather quinces pale with tender down,
and chestnuts, since we ourselves have loved these;
and you, O laurels, I will pluck, and you, myrtle, their neighbour;
since, so placed, you mingle sweet fragrances.
AS HE SPOKE TO OUR FATHERS, TO ABRAHAM, AND TO HIS SEED, etc.
As God had spoken by his own mouth to our fathers,

div.n: GLORIA PATRI, ET FILIO, ET SPIRITVI SANCTO.

lg.l: to great Abraham, and to his offspring and his descendants of old.
Thus the Prophets solemnly open their mouths as if by destiny,
we are sent hither, in our fallen state, to seek the oracles.
GLORY BE TO THE FATHER, AND TO THE SON, AND TO THE HOLY SPIRIT.
It is settled in the mind to render his due rights to the great Parent,
It is equally fitting for the Son, on account of the triumphs won over death,
As much as lies in our power, to give the deserved honors of praise,
And also the Deity proceeding from both Deities,
To celebrate in a similar manner, the will stands firm in the heart.
Maro's Muse sings the Hymn in paraphrase
COME, CREATOR SPIRIT, VISIT THE MINDS OF YOUR PEOPLE.
Come, kindly Spirit, sent down from high heaven,
Grant that you may enter these our dwellings as a new guest:
For to inhabit humble cottages, and unkempt countryside,
And the roof of a poor hut heaped with turf,
You desire, great in divine power, mangers pleasing to the Thunderer.
FILL WITH HEAVENLY GRACE THE HEARTS WHICH YOU HAVE CREATED.
Let this be your task, Life-giving Deity of heaven:
To breathe into the souls, which the right hand of the blowing breeze
Created out of nothing, the arms of your people for those striving,
And to have gifts on their shoulders, and to fix crests on their head,
To use the shield of grace, to bear the paternal emblem.
YOU WHO ARE CALLED THE PARACLETE.
You are able to soothe the sad sorrows of the mind,
By consoling with words and deeds to turn away cares,
A mind powerful in piety, preserved through a long age,
Not ignorant of evil, ready to help the wretched.
THE GIFT OF THE MOST HIGH GOD.
Shall I call you a gift, and equal you to better things?
Not equal to you is the scepter, which Ilione had once borne,
The eldest of Priam's daughters, and the necklace for the neck
Set with pearls, or the double crown with gems and gold;
You are the immense gift of the omnipotent Father of Olympus.
I would consider as nothing the gifts snatched from the Trojan ruins,
The ornaments of Argive Helen, which she from Mycenae,
When she sought Pergamum, and illicit nuptials,
Had carried away, the wondrous gift of her mother Leda.

div.n: FONS VIVVS, IGNIS, CHARITAS, ET SPIRITALIS VNCTIO.

lg.l: To these you may add a mantle stiff with figures and gold,
and a veil woven round with saffron acanthus:
All these things are nothing compared to the one gift of the Thunderer.
LIVING FOUNTAIN, FIRE, CHARITY, AND SPIRITUAL UNCTION.
You are the fountain of living water, leaping into the lofty
mountains of the heaven-dwellers, a fiery force, a flaming ardour
of a mind kindled by the love of God; and a fragrant unction
which brings back to you, sweating from the scented wood,
balsams that surpass the berries of the ever-leafy acanthus
by countless degrees: you, finally, the Godhead
are believed to be eternal, whom the stars of heaven obey.
YOU, SEVENFOLD IN GIFT.
You continually adorn your offspring with the sevenfold gift
in surpassing adornment: the lofty glories of the great parent,
the Royal Majesty has made common to the offspring.
YOU, FINGER OF GOD'S RIGHT HAND, YOU DULY THE PROMISE OF THE FATHER, ENRICHING THROATS WITH SPEECH.
You are the finger of the Father's right hand, you duly the Thunderer's
promise, enriching throats with the heavenly word.
KINDLE LIGHT IN OUR SENSES, POUR LOVE INTO OUR HEARTS.
Come, grant that ethereal light be kindled in our inmost senses,
so that a manifest taste may give proof, and the mouths
sad, of those who try it, be tormented by a bitter sensation,
and thus the mind turned away from God may learn its own deceits,
and then, no longer turned away, may obey, once the wiles are discovered.
As the wicked crow calls for rain with a full voice,

div.n: INFIRMA NOSTRI CORPORIS VIRTVTE FIRMANS PERPETI.

lg.l: And alone she paces by herself upon the dry sand,
As the various birds of the sea, and those which around the Asian
Search the meadows of Cayster in its sweet pools,
Vying with one another to pour abundant spray over their shoulders,
Now thrusting their heads against the waters, now running into the waves,
And you may see them exult with vain eagerness of lifting themselves;
Not otherwise is it to be desired that the fires of flames be sent
Into the cold minds of men, flames to lick the stars
And raise up globes, and melted hearts into the air.
Come then, blow through our heart with this vehement whirlwind,
And belching forth fires, mingle bedewing blasts.
STRENGTHENING THE WEAKNESSES OF OUR BODY WITH ENDURING STRENGTH.
Grant, Father, that the worn limbs of the weary body
Be strengthened with vigour, so that strength may return for battles.
We are overwhelmed by enemies: an iron shower assaults me:
Standing tall in the middle of the walls, the towering
horse pours forth armed men: others are present at the double gates,
As many thousands as never came from great Mycenae,
Others have besieged the narrow passages of the streets with weapons
Set against us: the line of iron stands, with gleaming point,
Drawn, ready for slaughter. Who, in blind warfare, could resist?
No one could; except those whom the Father of gods and King of men
Has breathed upon with the winds of the Spirit, and touched with fire.
MAY YOU DRIVE THE ENEMY FARTHER AWAY, AND GRANT PEACE FORTHWITH, THUS WITH YOU AS GUIDE GOING BEFORE MAY WE AVOID EVERY HARMFUL THING.
Drive hostile battle-lines far from here, drive arms far away:
We bear in our right hand the fillets and words of those who pray,
And a hand holds forth the branch of the peace-bearing olive.
Let treaties be joined, we all beg you for peace,

div.n: PER TE SCIAMVS DA PATREM, NOSCAMVS ATQVE FILIVM, TEVTRIVSQVE SPIRITVM CREDAMVS OMNI TEMPORE.

lg.l: Which may rest upon God, and be strengthened by the breath of the Godhead,
By which not every evil for the wretched, nor entirely all
Bodily plagues may depart: but wounded by sins
Hearts may be restored, with the deadly stain remitted.
GRANT THAT THROUGH YOU WE MAY KNOW THE FATHER, AND KNOW THE SON, AND BELIEVE IN YOU, THE SPIRIT OF BOTH, AT ALL TIMES.
With you as guide, it is lawful to know the Father, and may the serene
Face of the divine offspring, who this world with laws
Founded, may the power of seeing be granted to us.
And may all hold you from both to be the breathable Godhead.
That is of unmoved faith: cease to be moved by doubts.
GLORY TO THE FATHER, THE LORD, AND TO THE SON WHO ROSE FROM THE DEAD, AND TO THE PARACLETE FOREVER AND EVER. AMEN.
Praise to you, born of God, who triumph with death conquered,
By your own power departing from the tomb, and the Stygian marsh;
May great fame, with deserved trophies, sustain your
Name, may the good grace of your deed remain in the world,
At the same time let there be equal praise and glory to the immense Father,
And let there be to the one flowing from both into the ages his own Godhead,
Equal radiance, and grace, and splendor, equal summit of honor.

div.n: Quod in re diuina de Spiritu sancto proximè Euangelio præmitttitur, & Sequentia vocatur.

lg.l: What is placed immediately before the Gospel in the divine service concerning the Holy Spirit, and is called the Sequence.
COME, HOLY SPIRIT, AND SEND FORTH FROM HEAVEN THE RAY OF YOUR LIGHT.
Come, breath of the Godhead, from the shores of the heavenly homeland,
And let the quivering brightness of your light from the upper air
Come with a sound, let a mighty crash thunder upon the lands,
And let men recognize the promises of the supreme Father.
COME, FATHER OF THE POOR, COME, GIVER OF GIFTS.
Come, kindly Father; on your offspring, needy of all things,
Take pity on those poor in counsel and mind. With a generous
Hand you often heap the hearts of the wretched with gifts,
Rich in wealth, may you also be the author of a generous gift to me.
COME, LIGHT OF HEARTS.
Bring hither the light inaccessible to the rays of the sun,
Of the eternal Godhead, by which blind hearts may gleam.
BEST CONSOLER, SWEET GUEST OF THE SOUL.
Sweet relief, O Father, of every care and misfortune,
And as consoling a sick love with a hollow tortoise-shell.
Who else is more excellent than you in the duty of a guest?
REST IN LABOR, SWEET REFRESHMENT.
Rest in sweat; for hearts forgetful of their labors,
The nourishing breeze gives to its own a peaceful rest through their limbs.

div.n: IN ÆSTV TEMPERIES, IN FLETV SOLATIVM.

lg.l: He waters them, and those cherished in his bosom he soon raises to the lofty
groves of the heaven-dwellers, where soft marjoram them
with flowers, and, breathing, embraces with sweet shade.
IN HEAT, RELIEF; IN WEEPING, SOLACE.
And when the scorched field swelters with dying grasses,
Then, with the nearer divine power of God now breathed forth, the breeze
divine. With Zephyrs it tempers the fires of the stars.
And in his weeping, it is a great solace to the lover.
O MOST BLESSED LIGHT, FILL THE INMOST HEARTS OF YOUR FAITHFUL.
O light high in heaven, twice and thrice blessed on earth,
may you settle as a guest in the healed dwellings of the soul,
hiding yourself in the inmost depths of our mind.
WITHOUT YOUR DIVINE POWER THERE IS NOTHING IN MAN.
What, I pray, is the mortal race, if your Godhead is offended?
In vain will a friendly name be granted to the guilty,
unless, free from vice, to submit their necks to the Thunderer's
command they accustom themselves, and to execute the orders of Christ.
WASH WHAT IS FILTHY.
Come then, the minds defiled by deadly sin,
sprinkling with the rosy wave of precious blood,
wash clean, having now become milder with anger calmed.
WATER WHAT IS DRY.
Since dry things do harm, let the will stand firm to water the hearts,
let the South wind bring rains from the longed-for Olympus.
HEAL WHAT IS WOUNDED,
BEND WHAT IS RIGID,
WARM WHAT IS COLD.
Wounded, medicine with potent Paeonian herbs,
grant that it may restore the wounds, and let not Iapis heal me.
Let no advisor, however wise, persuade me
to move the earth when Boreas blows it stiff,
while winter shuts the fields with frost, and, when the seed is cast,
does not allow the frozen root to fix itself to the earth:
When the sturdy digger, wishing the stiffened acres
to turn, whatever I may do, in vain, pressing on he accomplishes nothing:
But you, Almighty, can do all things by your nod alone.
Bend what is rigid, even if there sounds with icy wings
Eurus and Notus rushing together, and, thick with storms,
Africus, and they roll vast waves to the shores.
Warm cold hearts. Let them grow warm with heavenly heat.
GUIDE WHAT IS ASTRAY.
And those whom to follow pathless ways in their course, at great peril,
you see, wandering, from the known region of the roads,
brought back to safety, driven by the turned North winds,
grant that I may see, and, with you as guide, rejoice in a favorable wind.
GIVE TO YOUR FAITHFUL,
WHO TRUST IN YOU,
THE SACRED SEVENFOLD GIFT.
The faithful hearts that follow the camp of your faith
and adore the supreme Godhead of the eternal God.
strengthen, O kind one, with the sevenfold vigor of your gift.
GIVE THE REWARD OF VIRTUE,
GIVE THE OUTCOME OF SALVATION,
GIVE EVERLASTING JOY.
Grant to the worshipper the honors which his own virtue promises,
and to close the completed day with a happy fate,
and for glad times to follow for the wearied mind,
so that together we may sing forever 'Io!' thrice, and the paean.
Hymn, SALVE REGINA.
Hail, you who walk as Queen of the Heavenly Ones, and at once
daughter and mother of God, enriched by so many triumphs won,
supreme mother of supreme mercy, our life, and salvation,
Hyblaean glory, and the trust of our race,
at the commands of the Heavenly Ones I shall bid you hail once more.
We have left the borders of our fatherland, and our sweet fields,
we wander, driven by the fates, around all the seas;
and homes in exile, lying beneath another sun,
we seek, alas, as fugitives, and the pitiable offspring of Eve.
O you who alone have pitied the unspeakable toils of men,
not unacquainted with misfortune, taught to succour the wretched,
who us, the remnants of Adam, both on land and sea,
now exhausted by all misfortunes, destitute of all things,
you associate in city and home: in our misery we call upon you in our prayers:
to you the offspring of Eve, in this tearful vale of toils,
sighing, and drawing its voice from the depths of its breast,
stands weeping, beseeching your divine power with strong groaning.
Therefore, kindly Mother, than whom none is more excellent
at calling upon God with her voice, and prevailing upon the supreme Father,
turn hither now your two eyes of ancestral mercy,
and the eyes of a merciful mind and of a Mother upon this
race of Christians turn, so that to behold Jesus
after this wretched exile of life, with the earth laid aside,
and may be able to gather the blessed fruit of your womb.
O clement, O loving of heart, O you who surpass in sweetness
sweet honey, glory and pattern of snow-white chastity,
great Mother of the Heavenly Ones, do not be loath to remember us,
so that your people, destined to come beneath the great vault of heaven,
to enjoy the promises of Christ through the long ages,
may exult, rendering eternal thanks for the gift.
WHOM EARTH, SEA, SKY, &c.
He who fills the sea, who fills the lands, who fills the heaven with his Godhead,
And who this threefold work, proud in its vast mass,
Sustains, by the mighty effort of his immense right hand:
And whom the heavens cannot contain within their spaces,
Him to inhabit humble cottages, and the hiding-places of the womb
It pleased, the adopted ones of Mary, and of the cloister of modesty
To keep unviolated the faith, and to consecrate chaste nuptials.
And He who the globe of the world, while Aurora in her rosy four-horse chariot
While she rises in the morning, illuminates with Phoebus's lamp;
But when evening is spent, when night now rushes from the Ocean,
Enveloping both earth and sky in a great shadow,
Supplies the shining Moon, and the radiant stars
By which you may return through the friendly silences of the quiet night;
Behold, in nine months, after the breathing Godhead
Had filled the womb of the divine mother with His Godhead,
By a happy birth he is brought forth into the shores of light,
Presently the infant emerging from the womb, while the stars marvel,
Comes forth most beautiful from the fragrant virgin rose.
O Mother too happy, twice and thrice blessed,
Who are heaped with so great an honor of a gift of the Heavenly Ones,
That He whom the vastest region of Olympus did not contain,
Should choose to be confined, that He may hide Himself in the sacred virgin.
Happy, celebrated by the melody of the Winged One's voice,
Who was sent to unseal the hidden springs,
Joyful in the birth of God, while Godhead overshadows with Godhead,
Pouring forth delights from the womb, and nursing hope at the breast,
By which the vows of the forefathers' desire are satisfied:
For you grant, O Virgin, that hope might have what it had hoped for.
Praise to You, who are sprung from the blood of the virgin Goddess,
With the heavenly Father, and the divine breath of the Godhead,
And to the threefold and one God be praise, equal power,
Let there be equal dominion, to which times that limits be set
Deny to be possible, since they are the rewards of an eternal kingdom?
AMEN.
HAIL, STAR OF THE SEA, etc.
Hail, starry glory of the sea, traversing the heavens,
Daughter of the highest Father, and at once nurturing Mother of your parent,
Splendor of the virginal flower, and of snow-white modesty
The eternal pattern, than which none is more excellent,
Unlocking the happy approaches of double-gated Olympus;
The sweet song of the messenger, from the sacred mouth of Gabriel,
things worthy to be told back to heaven. With the allied covenant of peace
Strengthen this offspring; and at the same time the ignoble name of Eve
Grant that it may gleam with the light of the rays of your race.
Turning hither and thither the immense coils of chains,
Do not hesitate to have loosed the guilty, confessing their offenses:
Surround blind hearts with the mantle of your sun.
Wherever a place, pitying our misfortunes, you
holds in the world, on whatever soil you reign most beautiful,
Always with my honor, always with my prayers will you be celebrated;
O be present at last, and look more closely upon things
It is lawful for you to ward off mortals from the perils of Cocytus,
Let it not irk your mind to succor wretched affairs.
Asking many gifts for your own, you will enrich the needy:
May the sweet face of the maternal Deity favor me,
And that compliant ears glide to your words
May you obtain [this] as a suppliant; nor the Deity unfriendly to me
allow to be, removing wrath from heavenly minds.
With you as Mother, may he be mindful that he was born of a virgin,
and given as a support of life to sick mortals.
O excellent Virgin, the confidence of our race,
adorned in mind with the distinguished honor of piety,
Us, freed from all the polluted dregs of crimes,
gentle in outstanding devotion, and of chaste heart,
Grant, I pray, to be adorned, with the redoubled ardor of the Deity.
Come now, divine Parent, I ask, direct our steps,
let it be lawful for the fleet to run a straight course on the clear sea:
Do not suffer it to wander adrift, with its Master lost,
but by the Mother's help let it sweep the blue waters unafraid,
Until it is permitted to rest in the longed-for harbour.
Where it may be lawful for the joyful to behold the holy face of the Deity,
And to sing an everlasting song with sweet melody:
Praise to you who are sprung from virgin blood. &c.
O GLORIOUS LADY, &c.
O ethereal glory, greatest part of the heavenly race,
Surpassing the Titanian stars with manifold light:
The almighty Creator, who you into the breezes of light
Brought forth out of nothing, like an infant licking sweet things,
Behold, once sucked the breasts in your sweet lap.
What she took away, breaking the commands of the highest Father,
Eve from her race (for whom she summoned the wrath of the Deity),
you restore to sick mortals by a happy birth.
Hence with weeping and sad laments far and wide the places once
those who filled with grief, now glad through divine gift,
by no means cease to cry thrice 'Io!', thrice 'Paean!'
And thus, Virgin, you become the gate of life to your offspring,
since through you they enter the heavens by the double-opening gates.
You the gentle approaches to the King, you the favourable times for death
solicit for your children, O thrice-greatest care.
Let it be right for you to be called those things, on this side by the title of gate, on that of window,
By name, let it be your right, by divine lot, to be called.
Applaud, O happy souls, for whom this auspicious gate
Of salvation opens. Grant to me also that the lofty halls
Of the heaven-dwellers be opened, for you are capable of all things by a nod,
As the Mother of the eternal Father, who has supreme power.
Praise to you who are sprung from the virgin blood of your mother,
With the heavenly Father, and the divine breath of the Deity,
And to the threefold and one God be praise, equal power,
Let there be equal dominion, to which the ages limits to be set
they would deny it to be possible, since they are the rewards of the eternal kingdom.
AMEN.
HAIL, QUEEN OF THE HEAVENS, etc.
Hail, holding the lofty sceptres of the heavenly crown,
Having ruled over the assemblies of the Winged Ones for so many years now,
O thrice-holy root, hail, by which from above to the world
The golden light arises, conveyed by rosy chariots,
Hail, gate of the heavens opening for the worshippers of Christ:
Rejoice, immortal glory of virginal modesty,
Outstanding model of beauty, surpassing the radiant
Stars, gleaming with much splendour beyond the rest,
Thrice-beautiful one, farewell, and with palms stretched out to the Godhead,
May it not displease you to entreat our salvation with prayers,
Granting by your prayers that we joyfully obtain the heavenly seat.
To the Blessed Virgin, Mother of God, for a happy departure from this life.
Virgin, powerful to soothe the grieving minds of men,
By consoling, and to turn away the cares of the wretched with words;
By those highest joys which seized your [heart],
When your offspring, living again, to the stars once more
Ethereal, and to have come beneath the upper breezes of heaven,
It was granted to you by lot to see, with death conquered;
I beseech you, do not refuse to help the doubtful affairs of the soul
Of your children, whom the anxiety of Erebus torments:
You see how, with a doubtful balance, the two scales
The ethereal Winged One carries, and the images of two
Souls placed upon them are carried, at once on this side and on that,
With a different sign, so that it may be revealed by a just distinction,
Which one wickedness condemns, and with great weight to Orcus
Presses down, or which one better virtue raises to the ether.
Alas, upon whom would the greatest horror of Hell not rush,
Uncertain where the fates may call, where it may be granted to stand?
Each one for himself, with crime made manifest, his own cause
Will plead alone, with the circle of those above and of men watching:
But He Himself in the midst of the Winged Ones, and of those flying in heaven,

div.note: On the scales of St Michael.
Uncertainty of salvation leaves us perplexed all our life.

lg.l: He will be King, and amid the light of the stars, on a flashing
cloud sitting, he will learn the lives and crimes of men,
what hiding-places will he not lay open here, and what hidden things,
he who grants to penetrate the inaccessible recesses of the mind?
Ah, how often, unknowing, under a false image of the true,
have I burst the breathing-passages of the soul with a deadly wound?
Has not a hidden error within, which escapes our notice, often
urged that an unspeakable war against the omens of heaven,
against the decrees of God, be demanded by a perverse spirit?
Perhaps the seeds of divine flame, given in vain,
lay hidden, concealed in the veins, and did not, deep in the heart,
flourish kindled in its bosom, and nothing worthy of heaven
did they do, and did not make others mindful of them by deserving well.
Ah, how often too, at the wave of the Lethean river,
drinking a liquid not truly carefree, and forgetfulness,
shall I be accused of forgotten duty, which must by right be expiated!
And so of God, not yet having sated its ancient grief,
the wrath will make us pay for our offenses with heavy punishment.
If they trembled, fearful with dread (they willed their own fates,
for the Saints were present), if horror stood around these,
whom their own virtue raised to the heavens for their merits;
what wonder is it that he trembles with fear, whom as guilty crimes
many weigh down? You will be struck, wretch, you will be shattered by the storm,
dregs of wickedness, a grim abomination will await you, a grim
punishment, and you will worship God with belated prayers,
unless the holy Virgin win by entreaty the aid of mercy for the one asking,
(the mother, surely, not terrified in spirit to no purpose,
and moved by the great peril of the struggling soul)
for rest is won for him, and the whole haven is at the threshold,
for whom the Star of the Sea calms the swelling sea with her prayers:
the innocent man will never be robbed of a happy death,
his breast protected by the heavenly prayer of Mary.
Come then, divine Parent of Christ, most holy, prophetess
foreknowing the future (if I ask for no undue
realms to my fates), since you can do all things by a nod,
Glory of the heaven-dwellers, grant that I may settle on Olympus,
where it may be lawful to be joined to Christ, and cherished by His countenance,
so that I cannot sate my mind, and may burn with gazing,

div.note: Cleanse me from my hidden faults, O Lord.
Saul is a witness to this.
How few can say with the Apostle: The grace of God in me has not been void. 1 Corinthians, ch. 15.
How many the help of the Blessed Virgin Mary has profited at the hour of death.

lg.l: Hanging in the embrace of the Offspring, and on the neck of the Parent,
While I fulfill the great love of the true Father.
Add at the same time erring men, and contrite hearts,
Who to retrace their step, and to escape to the upper air
Desire from the heart, and to tread in the footsteps of the saints.
Many a victim will fall before the altars of God by our right hand,
Duly likewise we will declare her own honor to the Mother,
Mingled with the clarions of the winged ones, and sounding lyres,
Striving to surpass the Nymphs with sweet melody,
To whom even Thracian Orpheus with his lyre would be compelled
To yield, when to the rhythms the seven distinct notes
He sounds in accompaniment, or strikes them with his fingers or an ivory plectrum.
AMEN.
